# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual specifies a defusal rule based on the cycling light and wire colours:
- Purple light -> cut green wire
- Red light -> cut blue wire
- White light -> cut yellow wire

I cannot speak, only gesture to Deaf. Blind cannot see gestures, only hear speech. Deaf can see the bomb and see my gestures, but cannot hear speech; however, Deaf can speak out loud, which Blind and I can both hear. Blind can touch and cut the wires, but cannot see their colours.

At this point in Turn 1, no convention or signaling code exists between Deaf and me. Deaf does not know what any arbitrary gesture would signify ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). If I wait, Blind and Deaf will speak first. Blind can describe what can be manipulated, and Deaf can describe the bomb's layout, wire colours, and the light's pattern, while establishing a gesture code for me to convey the defusal instruction.

Therefore, the appropriate action is to wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can cut wires 1, 2, or 3. Deaf will speak the bomb details next. Once you check the manual, gesture the solution to Deaf so Deaf can speak the wire number for me to cut.
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY is 0, LIGHT is white, WIRES are 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Mute, you cannot speak to Blind and Blind cannot see gestures, so gesture to me and I will speak the instruction to Blind. For wires: ☝ = cut wire 1, ✌ = cut wire 2, 🤟 = cut wire 3. Blind, tell us what controls you can interact with, but do not touch anything until Mute signals.

I have the defusal manual, which states:
- Purple light -> cut green wire
- Red light -> cut blue wire
- White light -> cut yellow wire
- "The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."

Deaf reported that in Round 1, the light was white, and the wires are:
1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue.

Blind cuts on Blind's turn. Because the turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf:
- If I gesture to Deaf in Round 2, Deaf will instruct Blind at the end of Round 2, and Blind would cut on Round 3.
- In Round 3, the light will have changed to the 3rd colour in the 3-colour cycle (not white). Cutting wire 1 then would detonate the bomb.
- By waiting through Round 2, Blind will not act (as Deaf instructed Blind to wait for instructions), and Deaf will observe and report the light's second colour at the end of Round 2.
- Then in Round 3, I can signal wire 1 (☝). Deaf will instruct Blind at the end of Round 3, and Blind will cut in Round 4.
- In Round 4, the 3-colour cycle returns to white (Round 1 = white, Round 2 = colour B, Round 3 = colour C, Round 4 = white), matching yellow (wire 1).

Therefore, I must wait this turn.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: UPDATE: The LIGHT changed from white to PURPLE! DISPLAY is still 0. WIRES are still 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Mute, I received NO gestures from you this turn! Remember: Blind CANNOT see gestures at all (Blind only receives blanks). You must gesture to ME (use to='deaf' or omit 'to'). I will speak whatever you signal to Blind. Signal now: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or 👍 / 👎 for button/other actions.

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, remember to send gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]) using the gesture symbol Deaf specified for the target wire. Bomb state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT purple, WIRES 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Deaf will speak the wire number to me so I can cut it.
Deaf says: Blind: Mute signaled ☝! Cut WIRE 1 (the first wire). Also, the LIGHT just turned RED. Blind, cut wire 1 now!

Let's analyze what happened and what the situation is:
- Manual rules:
  - purple -> cut green
  - red -> cut blue
  - white -> cut yellow
- "The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."
- Light sequence:
  - Round 1: white
  - Round 2: purple
  - Round 3: red (Deaf saw it change to purple in round 2, and in round 3 Deaf says: "Also, the LIGHT just turned RED.")
  - Wait, look at Deaf's message at the end of Round 3 (received at start of Turn 4):
    "Blind: Mute signaled ☝! Cut WIRE 1 (the first wire). Also, the LIGHT just turned RED. Blind, cut wire 1 now!"
- Wait! Blind acts on Turn 4 (right after Mute)!
  - Turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf.
  - In Round 4:
    - Mute acts now.
    - Blind acts next!
    - At the start of Round 4 / Blind's turn in Round 4, what is the light?
    - Deaf at the end of Turn 3 saw: "the LIGHT just turned RED."
    - Wait, does the light change every round?
      "It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of three colours."
      Round 1: White
      Round 2: Purple
      Round 3: Red
      Round 4: Back to White!
    - Wait, when does the light change?
      In Round 1, Deaf saw: "DISPLAY is 0, LIGHT is white"
      In Round 2, Deaf said: "UPDATE: The LIGHT changed from white to PURPLE!"
      In Round 3, Deaf said: "Also, the LIGHT just turned RED."
      Wait, Deaf said that at the END of Turn 3 (Deaf is monkey 3).
      Wait, did Deaf see Red at the end of round 3, or did the light turn red during round 3?
      Notice:
      Turn 1: Mute waited -> Blind spoke -> Deaf saw white.
      Turn 2: Mute waited -> (Blind did nothing?) -> Deaf saw: "The LIGHT changed from white to PURPLE!"
      Turn 3: Mute gestured ☝ -> Blind did nothing? Wait, Blind in Round 3 didn't speak? Wait, in Turn 4 arrival:
        Blind says to Mute: "Mute, remember to send gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...])..." - Blind spoke this during Round 3?
        Wait, in Round 3, Blind spoke BEFORE Deaf! Because turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf!
        So in Round 3:
        1. Mute gestured ☝.
        2. Blind spoke to Mute (Blind had not heard Deaf's response to ☝ yet, because Deaf goes 3rd!).
        3. Deaf saw Mute's gesture ☝, saw the light turned RED, and spoke: "Blind: Mute signaled ☝! Cut WIRE 1 (the first wire). Also, the LIGHT just turned RED. Blind, cut wire 1 now!"
- Now we are in Turn 4:
  - 1. Mute (me)
  - 2. Blind
  - 3. Deaf
- Blind has heard Deaf's message from end of Turn 3: "Cut WIRE 1 (the first wire)."
- BUT wait! What will the light be when Blind cuts in Turn 4?
  - If it changes every round:
    Round 1: White
    Round 2: Purple
    Round 3: Red
    Round 4: White!
  - If Round 4 has White light, what wire should be cut?
    "white | yellow" -> Wire 1 is yellow!
    Wire 1 is yellow! So when Blind cuts wire 1 in Turn 4, the light is WHITE, which corresponds to YELLOW! That is wire 1!
    Wait, let's verify:
    Is the light white in Turn 4?
    Round 1: White
    Round 2: Purple
    Round 3: Red
    Round 4: White!
    And wire 1 IS yellow!
    "WIRES are 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue."
    Wire 1 = yellow.
    White light = cut yellow wire!
    So in Turn 4, when Blind cuts wire 1, the light will be White, and Wire 1 is Yellow! That matches!
- Does Mute need to do anything in Turn 4?
  Blind already knows what to do because Deaf told Blind: "Blind: Mute signaled ☝! Cut WIRE 1 (the first wire)... Blind, cut wire 1 now!"
  Blind acts right after Mute in Turn 4.
  Mute cannot speak to Blind (Blind cannot hear Mute anyway? Wait, Mute cannot speak at all, Mute can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures).
  So Mute gesturing anything in Turn 4 would not reach Blind anyway. It would only reach Deaf, who acts AFTER Blind in Turn 4!
  Blind is about to cut wire 1 right now on Blind's turn!
  So Mute should just wait().

Let's double check everything:
- Manual:
  purple -> green
  red -> blue
  white -> yellow
- Light sequence:
  Round 1: White
  Round 2: Purple
  Round 3: Red
  Round 4: White
- Wire 1: yellow.
- At moment of cut (Round 4): Light is White, cut wire is Yellow (Wire 1).
- Blind has already been instructed by Deaf to cut Wire 1.
- Mute has nothing more to do, calling `wait()`.

```
wait()
```
